title: The goal line of a worker's brief says stop after 60 turns whatever cap dispatch gives
goal: bl_items.cmd_goal ends every goal text with a fixed 60-turn stop clause, so a research task or subtask dispatched with --max-turns 200 (ST-php5itob) or a story with 100 is told to stop at 60 whatever cap dispatch gives; the goal line of the brief names the cap bl_dispatch.max_turns gives the item (or --max-turns), so the brief and the session's limit agree. Found by the SP-qg7ncs6d review.

run: import subprocess,sys;r=subprocess.run(['python3','_tools/backlog.py','goal','BG-i4fxvd2h'],capture_output=True,text=True);sys.exit(1 if r.returncode or 'stop after 60 turns' in r.stdout else 0)

import re,subprocess,sys;f=lambda *a:subprocess.run(['python3','_tools/backlog.py',*a],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout;cap=re.search(r'--max-turns (\d+)',f('dispatch','--dry-run','BG-i4fxvd2h')).group(1);ln=[l for l in f('brief','BG-i4fxvd2h').splitlines() if ' is done: ' in l][0];sys.exit(0 if re.findall(r'stop after (\d+) turns',ln)[-1:]==[cap] else 1)
